events.note: Authored for credential-evidence#243 (Group D, D2 handoff) from the contract claims app-auth-token/app-auth-token-bearer-carrier, app-auth-token/app-auth-token-request-inputs, read on 2026-10-06 in this repository, without any scanner output. Carrier existence is provider-documented; the span and the value policy are project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence#243. Question: Which non-values around the app auth token can be asserted without taking a position on the app key? Options: Assert placeholders, references, masks and bare schemes only; or also assert a literal app key as public; or assert none. Decision: Assert placeholders, references, masks and bare schemes only; no literal app key. Reason: The contract records that Dropbox does not call the app key non-secret, so a literal app key would assert an unsupported public identifier. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's explicit instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases for these groups are authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2).
events.dissent: No dissent was raised. The strongest counter-argument, recorded because the rule asks for one: A placeholder in a client_secret field of a token request could be a mistyped literal in someone's script; the Case cannot tell them apart.
events.reversingEvidence: A Dropbox statement that the app key is public (to add it), or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
